title: Response Stability Index (RSI): calibration, monitoring, and deployment playbook
author: Marcus Chen
body:
Overview

This playbook defines the Response Stability Index (RSI): a lightweight, production-friendly metric for quantifying run-to-run output stability for generative models. RSI is intended to (1) detect quality regressions introduced by model updates, quantization, or serving-config changes; (2) surface workload-sensitive instability (e.g., long context vs short context); and (3) act as a gating signal in the model onboarding and promotion pipeline.

Why RSI exists

- Typical scalar quality metrics (BLEU, ROUGE, human NPS) miss nondeterministic variability and latency-dependent noise introduced by batching, KV cache behaviors, or mixed-precision kernels.
- RSI complements existing evals by focusing on variance and distributional consistency across controlled repeats and production shadow traffic.
- Designed to be cheap to compute and easy to integrate into alerting and model promotion automation.

Definitions and intuition

- Response Stability Index (RSI): a composite score (0.0 - 1.0) where 1.0 == perfectly stable (responses identical across repeats), and 0.0 == highly unstable.
- Core signals used: token-level normalized edit distance (NED), statistical entropy change per-token, top-k softmax mass variance, and latency-conditioned divergence.

RSI computation (summary)

1) For a workload W (set of prompts/prefixes representing a slice), run N repeats under controlled conditions (N recommended = 5). Repeats should vary only in runtime nondeterminism (e.g., different batch boundaries, same model weights).
2) For each prompt p and each pair of responses r_i, r_j compute token-level normalized edit distance (NED_{i,j}). Also compute per-token entropy H(r) using the model logits saved for the final pass when available.
3) Compute pairwise stability S_p = 1 - median(NED_{pairs}) after applying length normalization and trivial normalization (strip whitespace, normalize numbers).
4) Compute slice RSI as: RSI_slice = sigmoid( w1 * median(S_p) + w2 * (1 - median(entropy_variance)) + w3 * latency_penalty ), with weights w1=0.6, w2=0.3, w3=0.1 by default. The sigmoid rescales to 0-1.

NOTE: A reference implementation (Python) is provided in the eval-harness repo and used by the quality-guardrail-service. Integrations should prefer the canonical implementation to ensure comparability.

Reference RSI thresholds and actions

| RSI range | Meaning | Immediate action (auto) | Owner |
|-----------|---------|-------------------------|-------|
| >= 0.92 | Excellent stability | Promote candidate (if other checks pass) | Model Platform 
| 0.80 - 0.92 | Acceptable | Schedule canary with doubled shadow traffic | Model Owner 
| 0.65 - 0.80 | Degraded | Block promo; create regression ticket; trigger lightweight bisect (see triage) | Model Owner + Applied ML 
| < 0.65 | Unstable | Block promo; revert to last stable; emergency triage | Applied ML + SRE |

Note: thresholds are conservative defaults and must be tuned per workload slice. See Calibration section.

Calibration protocol (for new model families / quantization profiles)

Goals: define baseline RSI per workload slice and sensitivity profile for quantization or kernel changes.

Steps:
1) Select representative slices: short Q&A, long-context summarization (>2048 tokens), instruction-following, few-shot code generation. Use prompt catalog IDs from /eval/prompt-catalog.
2) Run baseline evaluation: N=10 repeats on the unmodified FP16 family across target hardware. Record RSIs and distribution of component signals.
3) Introduce the candidate change (quantized model, new kernel build, serving config). Run identical repeats.
4) Compute delta_RSI = RSI_candidate - RSI_baseline per slice.
5) Sensitivity rules:
   - If delta_RSI < -0.02 but RSI_candidate >= 0.90: flag for manual review (OK in many cases).
   - If delta_RSI <= -0.05 OR RSI_candidate < 0.80: fail automated promotion.
6) Produce a Calibration Report (template below) and attach to model-catalog entry and to the change request in the release pipeline.

Calibration Report template (fields)

- model_id, model_version
- hardware profile (GPU type, CUDA/cuDNN, kernel build id)
- workload slices (IDs) and sample counts
- baseline RSI per slice (median, 5-95 percentile)
- candidate RSI per slice (median, 5-95 percentile)
- delta_RSI and component diagnostics (NED increase, entropy variance change, latency_penalty)
- suggested action (promote/canary/reject)

Integration points and services

- eval-harness: orchestrates repeat runs; stores per-run logits and generated text in S3-like blobstore (bucket: s3://rwd-evals/logits).
- quality-guardrail-service: ingests RSI reports and stores time-series summary in TSDB (Prometheus long-term via remote_write or ClickHouse depending on volume).
- model-catalog: attach Calibration Report and mark promotion status.
- redwood-optimize: uses RSI deltas to suggest safer quantization profiles and batching recommendations.
- monitoring stack: Prometheus (metrics), Grafana (dashboards), Alertmanager (alerts).

Operational dashboards and alerts

- Dashboards to create:
  - RSI Overview: RSI heatmap by model family x workload slice over last 30d.
  - Slice Details: distribution plots of NED, entropy variance, per-prompt time series.
  - Serving Config Impact: correlate RSI with batch size, max_tokens, kv_cache hit rate.

- Recommended alerts (Alertmanager rules):
  1) RSI_slice < 0.75 for 5m sustained (severity: P2) -> notify applied-ml channel and create ticket.
  2) RSI_drop_delta <= -0.05 compared to 24h median (severity: P1) -> oncall page and paging.
  3) Repro-failure: variance between shadow and replay > threshold (P0) -> urgent SRE/Applied ML coordination.

Triaging regressions triggered by RSI

1) Reproduce: run the canonical eval-harness single-slice repeat with identical seed settings and N=10. If RSI reproduces, escalate.
2) Bisect: use automated regression-bisect tool (see /applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/automated-regression-bisect-and-blame-assistant-2026) to narrow commits / quant profiles.
3) Kernel/Infra check: confirm kernel build id, cuDNN, and GPU driver versions. Cross-check with kernel-and-scheduling docs.
4) Quantization sensitivity test: run quant-sensitivity suite (5 levels of quant) and compare delta_RSI.
5) Rollback/mitigation: fallback to last-stable model variant or increase sampling/caching to reduce nondeterminism.

Runbook: immediate mitigation steps (when RSI alerts fire)

1) Acknowledge alert in PagerDuty and post summary to #applied-ml-ops.
2) Run quick shadow replay for top-10 high-volume prompts. If RSI < 0.6 for these prompts, set immediate traffic kill switch on the model route.
3) If instability is correlated with a recent deployment, trigger rollback for that model-version using model-catalog automatic revert.
4) If caused by infra (kernel/driver mismatch), follow eng-infra incident flow and link to profile dump stored in S3.

Best practices and caveats

- Use representative slices. A global RSI can mask slice-level regressions.
- Repeat under production-like batching and with KV cache warm/cold states. Measure both warm and cold RSI.
- Watch for synthetic attack vectors: adversarial prompt perturbations can artificially reduce RSI; ensure prompt catalog integrity.
- RSI is additive to human eval; do not use as sole quality signal for high-risk customers.

Example RSI computation snippet (Python, pseudocode)

```python
import numpy as np
from textdistance import levenshtein

def normalized_edit_distance(a, b):
    return levenshtein.normalized_distance(a.strip(), b.strip())

def compute_rsi(responses, entropies, latencies, weights=(0.6,0.3,0.1)):
    # responses: list of N generated texts for a prompt
    pairs = []
    for i in range(len(responses)):
        for j in range(i+1, len(responses)):
            pairs.append(normalized_edit_distance(responses[i], responses[j]))
    median_ned = np.median(pairs)
    stability = 1.0 - median_ned
    entropy_var = np.var(entropies) / (1 + np.mean(entropies))
    latency_penalty = np.tanh((np.mean(latencies)-50)/200)  # arbitrary scaling
    raw = weights[0]*stability + weights[1]*(1-entropy_var) - weights[2]*latency_penalty
    rsi = 1/(1+np.exp(-12*(raw-0.8)))  # sharpened sigmoid around 0.8
    return float(rsi)
```

Onboarding checklist (tie into model promotion)

- Add RSI calibration report to model-catalog entry.
- Ensure eval-harness job id and blobstore pointer included in promotion ticket.
- If model has quantized variants, include per-variant RSI and suggested default profile.
- Confirm that quality-guardrail-service has a stored baseline and alerting rules for this model-family.

Ownership and contacts

- Metric owner: Applied ML (metric-owner: applied-ml-metrics@redwood.com).
- Oncall escalation: applied-ml-oncall (PagerDuty).
- Tooling and infra: eng-infra (kernel/build issues), eng-serving-runtime (runtime nondeterminism).
